about.title: About
about.lede: Two full careers — delivery and engineering — pointed at the same problem.
paragraphs: I build products end to end: the backend that has to hold up, the frontend people actually use, and — for the last three years — the AI layer in between.

The foundation is backend engineering. Seven years of Ruby on Rails, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Sidekiq and asynchronous processing in SaaS products for healthcare, insurance, logistics and compliance — the kind with real users, real SLAs and plenty of legacy code. On the front end I work with React, JavaScript and TypeScript, and I've shipped mobile with React Native.

Over the last three years I've been building with LLMs on top of that: document workflows in production, multi-agent pipelines in Python with tool calling and MCP, prompt design and evaluation, and the unglamorous part — cost, latency and what happens when the model returns something wrong.

Before engineering I spent eight years in quality management and IT project delivery at AT&T–DIRECTV, running project portfolios across Argentina, Chile, Peru and Uruguay. It's why I ask what outcome we're buying before deciding what to build.

I also run my own products under Orbital Labworks — Hausefy and Mottorfy. There I own everything: product, architecture, code, the platform integrations they depend on, and the infrastructure underneath. It's the fastest feedback loop I've found for becoming a better engineer.
about.philosophyTitle: What a software engineer is for
philosophy: The value of an engineer is not in typing code faster. It is in thinking, questioning and challenging assumptions before building: understanding the problem, weighing trade-offs, designing something that survives contact with production, and explaining it clearly to product, business and engineering.

A developer who only executes instructions is increasingly replaceable. An engineer adds judgment — pushes back when the scope is wrong, proposes better alternatives, protects maintainability, and ties technical decisions to real outcomes. That is the standard I hold on every project.
